high.title: Dollar-Won Closes at 1,530 Won, Tracking Yen Amid US Independence Day Holiday
high.summary: The dollar-won exchange rate closed at 1,530.00 won in overnight trading as of 2:00 AM KST on July 4th, representing a significant decline of 25.80 won from the previous Seoul foreign exchange market close. The move was notably driven by KRW tracking yen dynamics, highlighting the continued influence of JPY/USD on broader Asian FX sentiment. The US Independence Day holiday reduced liquidity, which likely amplified price action and contributed to volatility. For KRW traders, the sharp intraday recovery from earlier losses signals two-way risk in the current environment. The fact that KRW continues to shadow JPY movements underscores that any shift in Japanese monetary policy expectations or yen intervention rhetoric will have direct read-through implications for the won. Traders should monitor whether the 1,530 level holds as near-term support or resistance in the Seoul session open, and watch for any BOK commentary or smoothing operations if volatility persists.

high.title: NDF at 1,526.60/1,526.70 Won — Up 2.10 Won
high.summary: The dollar-won one-month non-deliverable forward (NDF) rose in New York overnight, last quoted at a mid-rate of 1,526.65 won, implying a 2.10 won increase relative to the previous Seoul spot close of 1,525.60 won after adjusting for the one-month swap point of -1.05 won. The bid/ask spread of 1,526.60/1,526.70 indicates relatively tight liquidity conditions, consistent with a US holiday session. For KRW traders, the NDF level provides a critical directional signal for the Seoul open — a firmer NDF suggests mild upward pressure on USD/KRW at the open. The swap point remaining in negative territory (-1.05 won) reflects the ongoing interest rate differential dynamic between Korean and US money markets. Watch whether offshore NDF positioning shifts materially heading into this week's Fed-related data releases, which could drive more decisive moves in spot KRW.

high.title: Treasury Bond Futures Mixed Amid US Holiday — 10-Year Down 3 Ticks
high.summary: Korean treasury bond futures posted mixed results in overnight trading with the US bond market closed for Independence Day. The 3-year KTB futures edged up 1 tick to close at 103.97, with foreign investors and financial institutions net buying 9 and 2 contracts respectively, while individuals net sold 11 contracts — suggesting modest institutional support at the short end. The 10-year futures fell 3 ticks, indicating mild steepening pressure on the Korean yield curve in a low-liquidity session. The divergence between the short and long end is notable: foreign net buying at the 3-year point may reflect continued positioning around BOK rate cut expectations, while the softness in 10-year futures aligns with lingering global term premium concerns. Bond investors should monitor whether foreign buying at the front end is sustained when full liquidity returns, as this would reinforce a bull-flattening thesis contingent on BOK easing. Watch upcoming BOK communications and domestic CPI data as key catalysts.

high.title: US Treasuries Rebound After Independence Day Holiday
high.summary:
US Treasury prices are recovering following the Independence Day holiday, with the 10-year yield pulling back to 4.464%, down approximately 2.20 basis points from the prior reference rate. The Treasury market had been under sustained selling pressure heading into the holiday break, and this post-holiday retracement suggests some tactical short-covering or renewed demand at elevated yield levels.

**Relevance for KRW and Korean bond traders:** US Treasury yield direction remains one of the most critical external drivers for Korean government bond (KTB) yields and KRW/USD dynamics. A pullback in the 10-year UST yield reduces upward pressure on KTB yields and can offer modest relief to the KRW by narrowing the US-Korea rate differential. If this UST rebound is sustained, it could support foreign inflows into Korean fixed income, a net positive for KRW stability. Traders should closely monitor whether the 4.46% level holds as near-term resistance or whether broader UST selling resumes — the latter would likely re-intensify pressure on the KRW and push KTB yields higher. Friday's US payrolls data will be the key near-term catalyst.

high.title: Fed's Waller — Forward Guidance Remains Valuable Policy Tool When Appropriate
high.summary:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller pushed back against incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's skepticism toward forward guidance, asserting at a European Central Banks conference that forward guidance remains a valuable monetary policy tool when deployed appropriately. Warsh has previously signaled discomfort with the practice, arguing it can generate market confusion and reduce Fed flexibility.

**Relevance for KRW and Korean bond traders:** This internal Fed policy debate has meaningful implications for global rate markets, including Korea. If Warsh's skepticism toward forward guidance prevails once he formally takes the helm, it would introduce greater uncertainty around the Fed's rate path, likely increasing USD volatility and complicating the BOK's own communication strategy. A less predictable Fed rate trajectory would make it harder for the BOK to calibrate its own easing cycle and could sustain elevated USD/KRW volatility. KRW traders should treat this as a medium-term risk factor — any ambiguity around the Fed's forward communication framework historically leads to EM FX underperformance, with KRW particularly sensitive given Korea's high export and capital flow sensitivity to US monetary conditions. Watch for further Fed speakers this week to gauge the balance of views.

medium.title: [New York FX Market Weekly] Japan's True Intentions Behind Yen Weakness — A Case of 'Reluctant to Ask, But Secretly Desired'?
medium.summary: This week's New York FX market focus centers on whether the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in 2025 and the likelihood of Japanese currency authority intervention. Speculation around a US holiday intervention by Japanese authorities fizzled out, with commentary suggesting that Takaichi may in fact prefer a weaker yen for domestic political and economic reasons. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is expected to begin a rate hike cycle at its July 8th meeting. For KRW traders, the yen dynamic is directly relevant — as demonstrated by Friday's price action where KRW tracked JPY movements closely. If Japanese authorities remain passive on yen weakness, Asian FX broadly, including KRW, may face continued depreciation pressure. The Fed rate outlook remains the overarching macro driver; any hawkish surprise in this week's US data could push USD/KRW back toward the 1,530–1,540 range.

medium.title: OPEC+ to Raise Output by 188,000 Barrels Per Day from August — Fifth Consecutive Monthly Increase
medium.summary: OPEC+ announced a fifth consecutive monthly production increase of 188,000 barrels per day starting August, bringing the cumulative supply addition since April to approximately 940,000 barrels per day. The decision was made by seven key members including Saudi Arabia and Russia in a virtual meeting. For Korean markets, lower oil prices are broadly constructive for KRW and the current account balance, as Korea is a major energy importer — cheaper oil reduces the import bill and supports trade surplus dynamics. However, if the oil price decline signals global demand weakness, the net effect on KRW could be muted or even negative through the risk-off channel. Bond investors should note that sustained oil price softness could contribute to lower domestic inflation, giving the BOK additional room to consider rate cuts — a modestly bullish signal for KTBs.

medium.title: Corporate Bond Issuance Off-Season Arrives Early – Market Recovery Not Expected Until Early Next Year
medium.summary:
Samsung Securities researcher Kim Eun-ki warns that Korean corporate bond issuance has slowed sharply in H1 due to elevated credit spreads and higher issuance costs, effectively pulling forward the typical year-end off-season. Recovery in primary market activity is now not expected until early 2026. For bond investors, this signals continued supply constraints in Korean credit markets, which may keep corporate spreads elevated relative to KTBs (Korean Treasury Bonds). Reduced corporate bond supply could marginally support KTB demand as investors rotate toward safer government paper, but the broader implication is that credit conditions remain tight for Korean corporates. Watch for any BOK policy easing signals that could catalyze a faster-than-expected recovery in issuance appetite heading into Q4.

---

medium.title: Homeplus Suppliers to Receive 300 Billion Won in Special Guarantees, 5 Trillion Won in Bank Support
medium.summary:
Following the termination of Homeplus's rehabilitation proceedings, the Financial Services Commission convened an emergency response meeting chaired by Vice Chairman Shin Jin-chang to contain potential financial contagion to the retail giant's supplier network. The FSC announced a 300 billion won (~$253M) special guarantee facility through the Korea Credit Guarantee Fund, supplemented by up to 5 trillion won in broader bank-level support for affected suppliers. While this is primarily a corporate/retail story, the FSC's rapid mobilization of state-backed credit facilities is marginally relevant to banking sector watchers — it signals authorities remain alert to systemic spillover risks and are willing to deploy policy tools swiftly. Fund managers exposed to Korean financials or monitoring policy bandwidth at the FSC should note this as a tail-risk management signal, particularly if Homeplus creditor exposure among mid-tier banks proves larger than currently disclosed. Watch for follow-up reporting on non-performing loan (NPL) impact at lender banks.

---

medium.title: US June ISM Services PMI at 54.0, Slows From Previous Month
medium.summary:
The US services sector remained in expansion territory in June with an ISM Services PMI reading of 54.0, though the pace of growth moderated from the prior month. The S&P Services PMI came in at 51.2, slightly below forecasts, reinforcing the narrative of gradual deceleration in US domestic demand. While still comfortably expansionary, the moderation reduces the probability of a hawkish Fed surprise in the near term. For KRW traders, softer US services data marginally reduces the risk of renewed USD strength driven by hot US growth momentum, offering a slight tailwind for EM currencies including the KRW. Korean bond investors should note that a cooling US services sector supports the case for eventual Fed easing, which would be constructive for KTB yields at the longer end.

---

medium.title: KOSPI Falls 0.46% as Foreigners Extend Selling Streak to 12 Sessions
medium.summary:
Foreign investors have now extended their net selling streak on the KOSPI to 12 consecutive sessions, with cumulative net foreign selling surpassing 38 trillion won. The benchmark KOSPI briefly touched the 7,800 level during the session before recovering to close above the 8,000 mark, down 0.46%. The KOSDAQ suffered a steeper decline, closing down 2.46%. The persistence and scale of this foreign selling pressure is a critical signal for KRW/USD dynamics — sustained equity outflows typically translate into KRW depreciation pressure as foreign investors repatriate proceeds. Fund managers should monitor whether this selling abates or accelerates, as a continuation could force the Bank of Korea to consider FX stabilization measures. The 38 trillion won figure in cumulative outflows warrants close attention as a potential catalyst for further KRW weakness.

---
